L2s leverage Ethereum’s EVM, token standards, and core assets like ETH, providing a consistent experience across L1 and L2. Users and developers can reuse the same wallets, tools, and code, while tokens retain a canonical L1 source of truth across rollups.

Rollups separate execution from consensus, enabling fast, parallel execution while inheriting Ethereum’s finality. A single proof replaces millions of redundant computations, making validation faster and cheaper.

High levels of profitability (e.g. 90%+ margins on Base). L2s pay usage-based fees in ETH when sending transaction data back to the L1, removing the need for a native-L2 token to facilitate economic security.

Recoverability: Users can withdraw their assets directly from the rollup to Ethereum through the L1 smart contract. This “escape hatch” ensures that, even if the rollup operator fails, users can recover their funds using data secured on L1—making rollups trust-minimized rather than dependent on a single operator.

Transparency: Rollups inherit Ethereum’s transparency by making their transaction data available on L1, allowing anyone to independently verify the rollup state. Even if the sequencer disappears or censors users, the full transaction history remains accessible and immutable on Ethereum.
